pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/src/decision/apply.ts:221 The apply driver asks for the whole Effects port (tx, blob, call) but only uses tx and call, so its one production caller (lib/decision/v1/applier.ts) has to pass an adapter that refuses `blob`; seams-and-adapters says the fix belongs here, in the consumer naming only the contract it uses.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/decision/apply.ts:221 applyNext and drainApplies take the full Effects but call only fx.tx and fx.call. The interface is one capability too wide, which pushes a blob-refusing adapter onto the applier.

packages/kernel/src/decision/apply.ts:244 Only the drain at the edge is async, and it is a bounded sequential loop. core.ts, apply-core.ts and the Tx-taking writers are synchronous.
packages/kernel/src/decision/apply-core.ts:43 The outbox state is one named value with an enumerated set of states, not booleans, and the TakePlan/FinishPlan unions are explicit.
packages/kernel/src/decision/schema.ts:191 SQL rows come back through a zod door (parseAt) rather than a type assertion. No `as` casts were found in decision/ or parts/.

packages/kernel/src/decision/core.ts:43 Core inputs are plain rows a test can build. No host-bound type has to be mirrored.

techniques.evidence: lib/decision/v1/applier.ts:62 The comment at lines 35-37 owns the choice, but the standard puts the fix in the interface: split Effects so drainApplies names only tx and call.
lib/decision/v1/types.ts:107 The adapter contract splits each source into pure packet/consequence halves and I/O read/apply halves.

lib/decision/v1/registry.ts:62 The registry restates the domain's source set as an exhaustive contract it owns. A new upstream source is a compile error, not a silent gap.
lib/decision/v1/types.ts:93 The one unsound step, method-parameter bivariance into DecisionAdapter<unknown>, is deliberate and comes with its written justification.
